races.title: State House, District 48
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Garland E. Pierce
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented North Carolina House District 48 (Hoke and Scotland counties) since 2005. Baptist minister and pastor for over 45 years, former UPS driver, and U.S. Army veteran (1971–1974). Graduate of Fayetteville State University and Shaw Divinity School.
cands.gaps: We could not find documented actions or stated positions from Pierce on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. The pages we read do not cover his sponsored bills in detail. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. His campaign site describes his service in general terms and states no policy positions. The sources do not name where he was raised or when he first lived in North Carolina, and the campaign site gives his birthplace as Fayetteville without naming the state. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements in the pages available.

local.label: Roots 55: His campaign site says he was born in Fayetteville and is a native of the Sandhills region, and records show him as a longtime pastor and a legislator for District 48 since 2005, living in Wagram; his upbringing is not documented, so the score rests on his decades as an adult in the state.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the North Carolina House since 2005 (21 years), including Appropriations and Commerce committee work. Also a Baptist pastor for over 45 years, a former UPS driver, and an Army veteran.
qual.why: More than two decades of actual legislative service puts him in the high band; committee seats and vice-chair posts were not counted, and no law, policy or budget career outside the legislature appears in the sources.

cands.name: Ralph Carter
cands.bio: Orthopedic surgeon in Laurinburg for more than three decades. Served 13 years of active and reserve duty in the Air Force. Born and raised in Wilmington, NC. Republican nominee for NC House District 48 in 2024 and 2026. Has not held public office.
cands.gaps: He has never held office, so there is no voting or legislative record to review. We found no stated position from him on data centers, and no statement on immigration enforcement or H-1B, abortion, or gun laws. The only land-related statements found were on his campaign site about water supply for Hoke and Scotland Counties and overdevelopment near Raleigh. His campaign site says he testified in Raleigh against diverting water upstream, and we could not confirm that independently. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. We found no news coverage of controversies and no foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign biography says he was born and raised in Wilmington, NC, and has lived in Laurinburg for 35+ years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Orthopedic surgeon in Laurinburg for over 30 years after 13 years of active and reserve Air Force duty. He has held no elected office; Ballotpedia lists him only as a candidate in 2024 and 2026.
qual.why: Long professional career, but in medicine rather than law, policy or budgeting. He has no legislative or local elected experience, which places him in the low band for writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: Long professional career, but in medicine rather than law, policy or budgeting. He has no legislative or local elected experience, which places him in the low band for writing law and the state budget.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says he will work to cap annual property tax increases as a first step toward possible reduction and elimination of property tax altogether, and to expand the homestead exemption for seniors.

land-for-floridians.evidence: His campaign site says he will work to stop corporate purchases of single-family homes and to reclaim North Carolina farmland from foreign countries.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he supports school choice so parents can select the best educational option, and that he will work to increase teacher pay and attract high-quality teachers.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he will fight for appropriations for more law enforcement officers, support tough-on-crime legislation including stiffer penalties for fentanyl distribution, and support higher pay and better benefits for first responders.
